fixes.explanation: Knocking on every door sounds like a very long day, friend. But the text doesn't mention any door knocking. The watchman sees the sword coming and blows the ram's horn to warn the people (Ezekiel 33:3).

Life. God says that if the man had heeded the warning, “…he would have saved his life.” (Ezekiel 33:5). The verse says heeding the warning is what would have saved him, not just hearing the horn. It's a serious line, so I'll just let it sit there.
The house of Israel. God tells Ezekiel, the man He is speaking to, “…I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). I bet that title hit hard.
Babylon is a fair guess, friend, but this verse doesn't name it. God says He has made Ezekiel a watchman “…for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). Those are the people on his watch.
Egypt is a fair guess, friend, but it doesn't come up here. God says He has made Ezekiel a watchman “…for the house of Israel…” (Ezekiel 33:7). That's who the warning is for.

That's right. If God says a wicked man will surely die and Ezekiel doesn't speak up, the man dies in his iniquity, “…yet I will hold you accountable for his blood.” (Ezekiel 33:8). That's a heavy part, and I think Ezekiel felt the weight of it.

Prayers and the proud don't come up in verse 11. What God says is, “…I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked should turn from their ways and live.” (Ezekiel 33:11). That's His answer to the people who asked, “How can we live?” (Ezekiel 33:10).
Learning is a fine thing, but it's not in verse 11. God wants “…that the wicked should turn from their ways and live.” (Ezekiel 33:11). The two words are turn and live.
Waiting is great for cookie dough, but it isn't what God says here. He wants “…that the wicked should turn from their ways and live.” (Ezekiel 33:11). The two words are turn and live, not wait.

Not quite, friend. God says “The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him in the day of his transgression…” (Ezekiel 33:12). He adds that the righteous man won't “…be able to survive by his righteousness on the day he sins.” (Ezekiel 33:12). So his past righteousness won't deliver him on that day.
Too slow is a fair guess, friend, but that's not their complaint. Verse 17 says, “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’…” (Ezekiel 33:17). Their charge is about justice, not speed.

Too strict is a fair guess, friend, but that's not the word they use. Verse 17 says, “Yet your people say, ‘The way of the Lord is not just.’…” (Ezekiel 33:17). Their charge is that it isn't just, not that it's strict.
False. God doesn't agree with them at all. He says, “But it is their way that is not just.” (Ezekiel 33:17). The charge gets turned back on them: it's their way that isn't just.

Tribe isn't in this verse, friend. God says, “But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 33:20). He says each of you, so He's speaking to people one at a time instead of as a group.

Family is a natural guess, friend, but it isn't the word here. God says, “But I will judge each of you according to his ways, O house of Israel.” (Ezekiel 33:20). The word is ways, and it's said to each of you.
